source.headline: Saudi Arabia submitted amendments to the Omani-Iranian proposal regarding Hormuz

summary: A Gulf official said Saudi Arabia submitted amendments to the Omani-Iranian Hormuz proposal because Riyadh was concerned the wording could establish a new status quo in the strait that would be unacceptable to Saudi Arabia and other GCC states. The update adds negotiating friction but does not itself constitute a breakdown in talks or a new shipping disruption.

learning_adjustment.basis: Current facts are only incrementally risk-negative because the postponement was already known. Leakage-safe v2 calibration shows strong performance for low-confidence MIXED/neutral signals and weak short-horizon performance for low-confidence directional calls; this supported keeping the forecast neutral rather than forcing a direction.

predictions.mechanism: Saudi objections add friction to Hormuz diplomacy and preserve geopolitical support for gold, but the information is incremental to the already-known postponement and does not yet create a fresh directional shock.
predictions.invalidation: A concrete Saudi-backed compromise on Hormuz would weaken the geopolitical bid; a breakdown in negotiations or new shipping disruption would instead turn the signal bullish for gold.

predictions.mechanism: Negotiating friction is mildly risk-negative through oil and inflation risk, but no new supply disruption has occurred and the prior postponement already captured much of the downside information.
predictions.invalidation: A clear Hormuz compromise plus lower oil would shift the signal upward; a collapse in talks with higher oil would shift it downward.

predictions.mechanism: High Treasury yields make growth equities sensitive to renewed oil-driven inflation, but the Saudi amendment story alone is not a sufficient new catalyst for a directional call.
predictions.invalidation: A material oil move tied to confirmed diplomatic progress or breakdown would provide a clearer directional signal.

predictions.mechanism: European equities remain exposed to high energy prices, while Saudi resistance to the draft adds uncertainty without yet worsening physical supply conditions.
predictions.invalidation: A concrete Hormuz accord and falling crude would turn the setup positive; renewed disruption would turn it negative.

predictions.mechanism: The update prolongs diplomatic uncertainty around a major energy route, but it is incremental and not enough to override the absence of a new physical supply shock.
predictions.invalidation: A signed or clearly agreed Hormuz framework would reduce the risk premium; a negotiation breakdown with higher crude would create downside pressure.
